text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong tells court he went into Cheng San GRC during the January General Election to expose Tang Liang Hong's dangerous views.
- A Japanese parliament member's landing on Senkaku islands has triggered immediate anger from Beijing.
- Young lawyer jailed for one week for contempt of court.
- Investigations by Commercial Affairs Department of two CAM International directors for alleged criminal breach of trust have started.
- Only one in every 1,000 Group A SingTel shares was sold last month despite their falling to all-time low price of Singaproe $2.37 apiece.
- Singapore gets 25 percent stake of Bangalore airport project costing S$640 million.
- Tokyo share prices soar to highest level in more than four months.
- Bre-X Minerals share prices fall close to zero after claim on Busang gold mine found to be a hoax.
- Property and electronics stocks take the lead in response to Wall Street's record-breaking climb.
- Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer announces monetary independence for UK central bank and an increase in bank rate to 6.25 percent.
- Jurong Engineering Ltd with two other partners getting final approval to build India power plan project costing S$691 million.
- CAM International buys raw material at 100 times the market price from supplier Watawa Precision Industries.
- Share prices of Uraco falls further after news of possible fraud at CAM International and confirmation investigation to follow.
- Share prices of Goodwood group to rise by S$3.68 while Hotel Malaysia share is expected to increase by SS18.94 through sale of Boulevard Hotel.
